newsitem.title: USA: NYC council says mayor asks to delay FY '98 budget.
newsitem.headline: NYC council says mayor asks to delay FY '98 budget.

text.p: The New York City Council said it plans to vote on Wednesday on a request by Mayor Rudolph Giuliani to delay submitting his preliminary budget for fiscal year 1998 until January 30.

John Banks, deputy director of the city council finance division, explained that the mayor asked the council to agree to the delay in the preliminary budget so that it can reflect the state's fiscal 1998 budget.

"More than anything else, it's just a timing issue, so that the mayor can incorporate more information," he said, New York State's budget, which is due before January 20, is expected to be disclosed by Gov George Pataki next week, possibly on Tuesday.
A spokeswoman for the mayor had no information immediately available to comment.

Giuliani also asked the council to let him send the mayor's management report, which will cover the city's performance during the first three months of fiscal 1997, on February 13, two weeks later than set forth in the city charter.

The charter also calls for the mayor to submit the preliminary budget on January 16, but the council official noted that it was not unusual for mayors to ask to submit their budgets late, and predicted that the council would approve Giuliani's request.
The mayor projected that the 1998 fiscal budget would total $33.49 billion when he reached the approximately $33 billion 1997 budget last June, Banks added.
